title: Find Customers Who Have Never Ordered
description:
Write a query to find customers who have **never placed an order**. Return `id`, `name`, and `email`.

**Hint:** Use a LEFT JOIN and filter for rows where the orders table has no match.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `amount`
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@email.com'),(2,'Bob','bob@email.com'),(3,'Carol','carol@email.com'),(4,'Diana','diana@email.com'),(5,'Evan','evan@email.com'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,150.00),(2,3,200.00),(3,1,75.00),(4,3,300.00),(5,5,125.00);
solution_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, c.email FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL

test_cases.description: Returns 2 customers who never ordered: Bob and Diana

hints: A `LEFT JOIN` returns all rows from the left table, with NULLs for unmatched right-table columns.
After the LEFT JOIN, filter `WHERE o.id IS NULL` to keep only customers with no matching order.
explanation: `LEFT JOIN orders` includes all 5 customers; for Bob (id=2) and Diana (id=4), there are no matching orders, so `o.id` is NULL. `WHERE o.id IS NULL` isolates those 2 customers.
